role: Illustrations of checked constructed mechanisms, not generated experimental observations

prompts:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: main introductory illustration for an AAMAS satellite-ground scheduling research paper. Generate a polished, high-information-density THREE-PANEL academic figure on pure white, ultrawide approximately 3:1 landscape. Crisp print-quality sans-serif typography, no gradients behind text, no watermark, no company logo. Colors: evidence/feasibility blue #176B9B, interventions orange #D36B32, synthesis purple #71559C, context slate #687782. Consistent line weights. Attractive restrained isometric satellites and ground antennas, with exact flat mathematical graph insets, not a generic box-and-arrow flowchart.
Panel (a), left quarter: title 'Satellite-ground contacts'. Two satellites above a curved Earth limb, two ground antennas G1 and G2, separate blue/orange contact beams, beneath them a compact shared-resource timeline with visible occupied contact intervals and an orange gap ruler. Label 'Same contacts and rewards' and 'Ground gap: 0 -> 4'. Show one clock slider changing clearance while opportunities remain fixed. Illustrative physical setting, not actual orbital imagery or measured dataset.
Panel (b), center half: title 'One intervention, two different completions'. Two fully explicit graph insets side by side, headings 'gap = 0' and 'gap = 4'. Both contain exactly eight nodes: roots a,b (reward 8 each), X1,X2,X3 on a side and Y1,Y2,Y3 on b side (reward 6 each). Edges in BOTH graphs: a-b; a-X1,a-X2,a-X3; b-Y1,b-Y2,b-Y3; Y1-Y2. BEFORE graph has no X-X edges. AFTER adds exactly X1-X2,X1-X3,X2-X3, highlighted orange; all other edges unchanged. NO other edges. Place roots centered, X group upper-left, Y group upper-right, legible node names. Under each show two feasible residual alternatives after forcing a or b, with chosen nonneighbors softly highlighted: BEFORE 'Force a: 20' and 'Force b: 26'; AFTER 'Force a: 20' and 'Force b: 14'. Root a leaves the Y group where at most two chosen; root b leaves X group where before three and after one can be chosen. These are mathematically exact constructed illustration values, not empirical performance.
Panel (c), right quarter: title 'Why the input must change'. Equal-height cards for a and b marked 'Same base inputs' and a large orange equality sign; below a purple small neighborhood lens showing edge counts 'X: 0 -> 3' and 'Y: 1 -> 1'. Clear blue conclusion 'Preferred action: b -> a'. Bottom unobtrusive tag 'Constructed, certified illustration'. Do not add charts or fabricated experimental wins. Use large legible short text; balance spatial narrative and rigorous graph detail. Keep all listed edge topology and numbers EXACT. No long prose.

Edit the supplied generated research illustration; preserve the attractive satellite/Earth/antenna scene, white background, exact overall three-panel layout, sizes and palette. Correct only mathematical content. In panel (b), KEEP the two large eight-node graphs but make their topology exact: both graphs contain a-b; a-X1,a-X2,a-X3; b-Y1,b-Y2,b-Y3; and ONLY one Y-to-Y edge Y1-Y2. There must be NO Y2-Y3 and NO Y1-Y3 edge. The gap0 graph has NO X-to-X edges. The gap4 graph has exactly the three orange X-to-X edges X1-X2, X1-X3, X2-X3. Keep all roots labeled reward8, every peripheral reward6. DELETE all four small lower graph insets entirely, including their incorrect extra numbers/duplicated names. Replace that lower area with four clean compact selection strips, two under each large graph, using chips for selected vertices and a short equation, NO graph edges. Gap0 strips: 'Force a' then chips 'a  Y1  Y3', then '8 + 6 + 6 = 20'; 'Force b' then chips 'b  X1  X2  X3', then '8 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 26'. Gap4 strips: 'Force a' then chips 'a  Y1  Y3', then '8 + 6 + 6 = 20'; 'Force b' then chips 'b  X1', then '8 + 6 = 14'. Mark 'Prefer b' below gap0 and 'Prefer a' below gap4. No other numbers in these strips. In panel (c), replace the two base-input cards with IDENTICAL numeric fields for a and b: 'weight = 8', 'degree = 4', 'neighbor weight = 26'. Keep equality between them. Keep neighborhood counts X0->3,Y1->1 and preferred b->a. Preserve bottom label 'Constructed, certified illustration'. This is an exact explanatory motif, no experimental-performance chart. Ensure very legible short sans-serif text and unchanged rich physical panel.

Edit only the TWO LARGE CENTRAL GRAPH INSETS in this image. Preserve EVERYTHING ELSE exactly: satellites, Earth, timeline, headings, all four correct selected-vertex chip strips/equations, preference labels, right-side input cards. The current graph drawings wrongly imply an extra Y2-Y3 edge and place the X clique collinearly. Redraw just those central graph insets in a clean NONCOLLINEAR layout so topology is unambiguous. Each inset has exactly roots a,b at the bottom centre, three X vertices on left in a triangle layout, and three Y vertices on right with Y1 and Y2 aligned HORIZONTALLY at top and Y3 farther right below, separated from both. Connect a-b. Connect a to each Xi. Connect b to each Yi. In BOTH insets, the ONLY edge between Y vertices is a SHORT HORIZONTAL segment Y1-Y2 at the top. Y3 has exactly ONE incident edge: its diagonal spoke to b. There must be no Y2-Y3 or Y1-Y3 segment, even faintly. In gap0 there is NO X-X edge. In gap4 all three X-X edges form an orange NONCOLLINEAR TRIANGLE around the three X nodes, each Xi additionally retains its spoke to a. No other edge. All peripheral nodes reward6, roots reward8. Do not change the chip-strip memberships or arithmetic. This is mathematical accuracy repair, not a style redesign.

prompts:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: dense mechanism illustration for an AAMAS paper titled LLM-Guided Synthesis of Constraint-Adaptive Heuristics for Satellite-Ground Scheduling. Generate an elegant print-ready WHITE-background ultrawide THREE-PANEL landscape academic illustration, approximately3:1. It should visually explain computation and LLM's actual role, not just generic boxes. Colors blue#176B9B evidence, purple#71559C synthesis, orange#D36B32 obstruction/unknown, slate#687782 context; crisp large readable sans-serif text. No company logos, fabricated plots or empirical performance numbers.
LEFT PANEL title '(a) Certified evidence'. Two residual-world illustrations after forcing competing actions: a blue contact chip 'a:8' above a slate disconnected five-node cycle K and an isolated blue node A with label 'A:5'; next to it 'b:6' above an IDENTICAL five-node cycle K and isolated node B labeled 'B:2'. Each K is a five-cycle of reward10 nodes; label under both jointly 'Same unqueried component K'. A blue mathematical strip 'Delta = (8+5) - (6+2) = 5', and 'K cancels exactly'. Small overlapping bound strips labelled 'a: [33,43]' and 'b: [28,38]', no axis or fictitious data. Beneath is a tiny orange equality-class witness: strict a->b collapses because 'phi(a)=phi(b)', creating an orange self-loop on class C; label 'Missing distinction'. This is a constructed explanatory example, not a measured scheduling benchmark.
CENTRE PANEL title '(b) Offline LLM synthesis'. A polished purple schematic reasoning-agent icon, like a compact open notebook with graph fragments and a neural-network lens, not a humanoid robot or commercial logo. The INPUT beside it comprises three stacked readable cards: 'Graph + boundary', 'Certified preferences', 'Equality-join witness'. A compact prompt excerpt in quotation-card styling: 'Find a structural distinction. Compose typed features and a scoring rule.' Under the icon, show two alternative typed compositions as clean compact operation diagrams: root -> neighbors -> induced_edges -> count, and root -> neighbors -> clique_cover_weight. Use connected purple operation tiles with literal type annotations 'Node', 'NodeSet', 'EdgeSet', 'Number' where appropriate. Mark 'LLM proposes; tools verify'. No claim the LLM itself certifies optimality or feasibility.
RIGHT PANEL title '(c) Checked program, frozen deployment'. At top a two-column manuscript/code card labelled 'Feature-rule candidate' with EXACT text 'nc = clique_cover_weight(neighbors(root))' and 'score = w / max(eps, w, nc)'. Beside it small blue verification checklist: 'Full quotient', 'Complete schedule', 'Measured cost'. Then a prominent blue/purple freeze seal and divider labelled 'OFFLINE | ONLINE'. Below show a conflict-graph node selection with selected nodes highlighted blue, conflicting nodes gray, and a compact ground-station timetable of nonoverlapping blue contacts. Arrows depict 'Score -> commit -> residual update' and 'Fixed feasibility kernel'. Bottom large assurance 'No online LLM or oracle'. Overall rich coherent visual narrative with restrained satellite/contact icon cues linking to physical scheduling; no oversized decorative emptiness. Fit all text legibly; do not add extra formulas, confidence values, win claims or arbitrary experiment results. Strong graphical emphasis on the passage from a proven information obstruction to generated executable structure and then checked/frozen deployment.
